newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas falls despite cold in West.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas falls despite cold in West.

text.p: Canadian spot natgas prices were sharply lower in the western markets Monday, ladened by a weak demand from the East and the return to service of a British Columbia gas plant over the weekend, sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices fell nearly 30 cents from Friday's levels into the C$1.35-1.40 per gigajoule (GJ) range despite the continuing cold in western Canada.

"NOVA packed over the weekend, and TransCanada is only taking 6.3 bcf (billion cubic feet) out of the border," one Calgary-based trader said, noting the pipeline's average takes out of the border are almost 6.5 bcf.
Temperatures in Calgary are expected to reach only highs of -9 to -12 degrees Celsius until Friday.
April AECO prices were talked around C$1.40 per GJ.
At Sumas, Wash., prices slumped into the $1.10-1.15 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) area, down about 10 cents from Friday.
Sources attributed to the softness to the return to service of Westcoast Energy's McMahon gas plant in B.C. on Saturday.
Last week, the company declared a force majeure, which affected about 170 million cubic feet per day of production.

At Niagara, prices drifted into the $2.03-2.08 per mmBtu range, down about four cents from Friday, as forecasters called for milder weather later this week and buyers were able to take advantage of the ample storage supplies.
